newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hysan sees more active property market.
newsitem.headline: Hysan sees more active property market.

text.p: Hysan Development Ltd said on Friday it was on track to reap the benefits of a more active property market this year.
"The prospects for the luxury residential sector continue to look favourable," the company said in its interim report.
"There have been continuing signs of increased activities for the leasing of grade A offices, and rentals are likely to continue to recover gradually after a period of consolidation."
Hysan reported profit attributable to shareholders of HK$697.45 million for the first six months of 1996, an 10.31 percent increase over the corresponding period last year.

The rise came on the back of a 13 percent increase in turnover to HK$1.11 billion. Earnings per share were HK$0.6781, a 7.74 percent increase, slightly lower than the net increase due to the conversion of warrants during the year.
The report said that the company's rentals of luxury residential properties continued to improve.
The office leasing market had been more active, but the company said that rental levels for office space had remained mostly unchanged during the first six months of the year.

The group's only project under development in Hong Kong, the old Lee Gardens Hotel which is being redeveloped into an office and retail complex, is scheduled for completion in the first quarter of 1997, the report said.
The new building will have a total of 900,000 sq ft of space, and will increase the group's portfolio of properties by 23 percent.
The report also provided an update on five overseas development projects in which the group has taken stakes ranging from 10 percent to 50 percent.
Of these, only Melville Park residential development in Singapore, in which the group has a 10 percent interest, has been sold, the report said.
Hysan is also participating in two developments in Shanghai, the Peace Garden which is purely residential and the Grand Gateway which is a multi-function building.
